bullet_points: Load the tracer trajectories (`traj_x.npy`, `traj_y.npy`) and time array (`t_traj.npy`).
Unwrap the periodic trajectories (domain $L=2\pi$) to compute continuous absolute displacements, and save these unwrapped trajectories to disk for use in later steps.
Compute the Mean Squared Displacement (MSD) as a function of lag time $\tau$, fit a power law to extract the superdiffusive exponent $H$, and print the numerical value to verify $H \approx 0.88$.
Compute displacement vectors $\Delta \mathbf{x}(\tau)$ for a range of time lags $\tau$.
For each $\tau$, compute the empirical characteristic function $\phi(k, \tau)$ and estimate the stable index $\alpha(\tau)$ by fitting it to the model $\exp(-|Dk|^\alpha)$.
Compute Lagrangian velocities using finite differences of the unwrapped trajectories.

Compute the velocity increment PDF $\delta v(\tau) = v(t+\tau) - v(t)$ for several lag values $\tau$, test whether the tails are power-law distributed by fitting a tail exponent, and print the results.
Compute the Lagrangian velocity autocorrelation $R_v(\tau)$.
Save the computed MSD, $H$, $\alpha(\tau)$, $R_v(\tau)$, velocity increments, and displacement distributions for selected $\tau$ to disk as `.npy` or `.npz` files.
sub_tasks.sub_task: Compute Lagrangian Displacement Statistics, Velocity Autocorrelation, and Velocity Increments

bullet_points: Load the Eulerian vorticity fields (`vorticity_snapshots.npy`) and snapshot times (`snap_times.npy`).
Using spectral derivatives (FFT), compute the streamfunction, velocity components, and velocity gradients to calculate the Okubo-Weiss parameter $Q$ for each snapshot.
Define masks for vortex cores ($Q < 0$) and strain regions ($Q > 0$).

Print the fraction of the domain area classified as vortex-dominated ($Q < 0$) versus strain-dominated ($Q > 0$) for each of the 15 snapshots, and print the mean and standard deviation of the $Q$ threshold used.
Compute the isotropic energy spectrum $E(k)$ from the velocity fields.
Compute and print the spectral slope of $E(k)$ in both the large-scale (inverse cascade) and small-scale (enstrophy cascade) ranges separately, with explicit wavenumber ranges used for each fit.
Save the $E(k)$ spectrum, $Q$ fields, and the vortex/strain masks to disk.
sub_tasks.sub_task: Compute Eulerian Flow Characterization and Vortex Identification

bullet_points: Load the wrapped trajectories, the unwrapped trajectories (from Step 1), the $Q$ fields (from Step 2), and the snapshot times.
Map each tracer's wrapped position to the Eulerian grid to extract the local $Q$ value at the 15 snapshot times.
Note and print the temporal resolution mismatch (snapshots are 40 time units apart, trajectories are 0.4 time units apart).
Use nearest-neighbor assignment in time to assign a continuous state to each tracer at each time step (Vortex if $Q < 0$, Strain if $Q > 0$).

Compute and print the fraction of total trajectory time-steps classified as Vortex versus Strain across all tracers, and compute the fraction of tracers that are predominantly (>50% of their time) in each state.
Compute conditional displacement PDFs and conditional MSD for the Vortex and Strain populations using the unwrapped trajectories.
Identify trapping events (consecutive time steps in the Vortex state) and extract their durations $\tau_{trap}$.
Compute the jump size distribution $P(\Delta x)$ during free-flight (Strain) periods separately from trapping (Vortex) periods, and fit power-law tails to both distributions.
Compute velocity increments $\delta v(\tau)$ and normalize them by the local RMS velocity of the respective region.
Identify large jumps (e.g., >3 standard deviations) and compute statistics on whether they correlate with exit events from vortex cores (transitions from Vortex to Strain).
Save all conditional statistics, trapping times, and jump statistics to disk.
sub_tasks.sub_task: Compute Tracer State Partitioning, Conditional Statistics, and Trapping Times

bullet_points: Load the results saved in Steps 1 and 2.
Plot the displacement PDFs $P(\Delta x, \tau)$ for multiple lags, showing the transition from Gaussian to heavy-tailed behavior, and overlay a reference Gaussian curve on each displacement PDF panel.
Plot the estimated stable index $\alpha(\tau)$ versus $\tau$.
Plot the Lagrangian velocity autocorrelation $R_v(\tau)$ and check for power-law decay.
Plot the energy spectrum $E(k)$ to verify the inverse energy cascade, and overlay reference power-law slopes (e.g., $k^{-3}$ and $k^{-5/3}$) with explicit annotations of the fitted slopes.
Plot a representative snapshot of the vorticity field overlaid with contours of the Okubo-Weiss parameter $Q$.
Save all plots as high-resolution PNGs.
sub_tasks.sub_task: Plot Lagrangian Statistics, Velocity Autocorrelation, and Eulerian Fields

bullet_points: Load the results saved in Step 3.
Plot the conditional displacement PDFs and conditional MSD, comparing the Vortex and Strain populations.
Plot the distribution of trapping times $P(\tau_{trap})$ and perform a power-law fit to estimate the exponent $\mu$.
Plot the normalized velocity increment PDFs for both regions.
Plot the jump size distribution $P(\Delta x)$ for both Vortex-exit events and general Strain-region displacements on the same axes, with power-law fits overlaid.
Print detailed statistics regarding the correlation between large jumps and vortex exit events.
Save all plots as high-resolution PNGs.
sub_tasks.sub_task: Plot Conditional Statistics, Trapping Times, and Jump Distributions

bullet_points: Review all generated plots and printed statistics from the previous steps.
Write a comprehensive Results section for a scientific paper.

Tabulate all key quantitative results ($H$ exponent, $\alpha(\tau)$ range, $\mu$ exponent for trapping times, spectral slope, fraction of time in vortex vs. strain, fraction of large jumps coinciding with vortex exits) in a summary table within the Results section.
Discuss the robustness of the heavy tails and the evolution of $\alpha(\tau)$.
Interpret the Eulerian flow characteristics and the validity of the tracer partitioning.
Analyze the conditional MSD and displacement PDFs to determine if heavy tails are intrinsic to the strain field or a consequence of vortex trapping/ejection.
Discuss the trapping time distribution and its implications for the Continuous-Time Random Walk (CTRW) mechanism.
Conclude on the primary physical mechanism responsible for the anomalous diffusion (CTRW vs. direct Lévy vs. fractional Brownian motion).
